name: Particle Swarm Optimization
miniText: How can shared memories guide a population toward high-valued locations? NetLogo Particle Swarm Optimization gives each particle a position, velocity, personal best, and information about the swarm's best discovery. Kennedy and Eberhart [1] provide the originating algorithm, Shi and Eberhart [2] modify velocity control, and Clerc and Kennedy [3] analyze stability and convergence. Their work frames the balance between exploration and attraction to previously successful positions. The NetLogo Info explicitly describes adaptations for a wrapping two-dimensional world and a grid-valued objective, so it is a principle demonstration rather than an exact numerical replica of the original optimizer. Velocity settings, random influences, initialization, and the landscape affect success. Reaching a good displayed peak does not prove global optimality or validate the same parameters for continuous high-dimensional optimization.
